title: throughput-spline-annotated-runlog-may10-2026
content:
Summary:
This runlog captures a small-scope benchmark exploring how request payload compaction + streaming chunking interacts with throughput curves and tail latency under mixed session workloads. The goal: find low-friction engineering knobs that reduce $/token while preserving p90/p99 service-level behavior for interactive chat-style sessions.

High-level takeaways:
- Compact binary payloads (protobuf-lite) reduce median and tail latencies modestly and reduce CPU serialization overhead, translating into ~18–28% lower infra cost in throughput-limited regimes.
- Streaming chunking (emit-as-available) shifts p50 down further but can increase p99 in high-coalescence cases unless prefetching is tuned.
- KV-cache hit rate has a nonlinear effect: moving from 60%->85% hit reduces p99 by ~35% in these tests (sessionized workload).
- Best single change: enable protobuf-lite + streaming + conservative prefetch (prefetch 1 next segment) — net measured $/1k tokens dropped ~26% with p99 impact within +5–8% of baseline.

Methodology:
- Cluster: 4 x G5.12xlarge-equivalent serving nodes (model: open-llm-v1-7b, fp16 static quant)
- Workload generator: synthetic session mix derived from production histograms (70% short queries < 40 tokens; 30% long sessions 200–1200 tokens).
- Duration: 4 hours for each scenario; steady-state window = last 2 hours.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, CPU% on host, network bytes, and infra $ estimate using Redwood pricing model (compute + memory amortization + egress).

Scenarios tested (names used below):
- baseline-json: default JSON body, no streaming, default batching
- protobuf-compact: compact protobuf payload, no streaming
- stream-json: JSON body but using streaming responses chunked at 128-token boundaries
- stream-proto-prefetch: protobuf + streaming + prefetch=1
- stream-proto-aggressive: protobuf + streaming + prefetch=3

ASCII result table (steady-state window aggregated):
Scenario | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/s | $/1k tokens
baseline-json        | 92   | 245  | 540  | 320  | $0.029
protobuf-compact     | 78   | 200  | 430  | 360  | $0.023
stream-json          | 70   | 210  | 610  | 410  | $0.025
stream-proto-prefetch| 62   | 185  | 450  | 430  | $0.021
stream-proto-aggressive| 58 | 170  | 520  | 460  | $0.020

Interpretation notes on the table:
- protobuf-compact shows a clear median and p90 improvement vs baseline with lower cost because payloads are ~40% smaller, reducing network serialization/deserialization and host CPU pressure.
- stream-json lowers p50 and improves throughput (client-side latency masking) but increases p99 — likely due to head-of-line scheduling interaction and the extra pressure on the runtime when many small chunks are queued.
- prefetch tuning mitigates the p99 spike: prefetch=1 trades a bit more work for the worker while keeping tail under control. prefetch=3 improves p50/p90 but again risks p99 regression in high-concurrency experiments.

Throughput-spline sketch (textual):
- X-axis: offered load (rps normalized to tokens/s), Y-axis-left: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), Y-axis-right: $/1k tokens.
- Observed spline shape: p50 increases almost linearly with offered load; p90 starts to bend upwards at ~380 tokens/s; p99 shows exponential growth after ~420 tokens/s for baseline-json.
- With protobuf-compact, the bending threshold shifts right by ~20–55 tokens/s; with streaming+prefetch it shifts further right (higher sustainable throughput).

Micro-investigations (short notes):
1) Serialization CPU vs network: Profiling showed JSON parse/encode was ~1.8x the CPU cost of protobuf-compact per request on average. During bursts, CPU stalls correlated strongly with p99 spikes.
2) Chunk queueing: runtime multiplex queue lengths spiked under stream-json at high concurrency; adding per-connection chunk backpressure reduced p99 by ~12% but lowered throughput by ~6%.
3) KV cache interaction: when KV hit rate fell below 65% because of session sharding mismatch, p99 rose rapidly; adding a lightweight session-affinity gate improved cache efficiency and smoothed tails.

Cost model example (simplified):
- Baseline (per 1M tokens): compute+mdev = $29; with protobuf+stream-prefetch = $21; rough saving ~28%.
- Note: savings sensitive to egress pricing and client-side compression — if clients already gzip payloads, protobuf advantage shrinks to ~10–12%.

Risk and caveats:
- Protobuf adoption requires client changes; rollout must consider backward compatibility and a staged canary.
- Streaming affects consumer integration patterns (UI logic expecting full response). We should offer both streaming and non-streaming endpoints for 3 months during rollout.
- Prefetching tuning is workload-dependent and needs per-tenant knobs. Over-aggressive prefetch can waste GPU compute on unused segments.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Engineering spike: implement protobuf-lite server-side + compatibility layer (2 sprint estimate). Owner: Max Chen.
- Instrumentation: add chunk-queue depth and per-connection prefetch metrics to Console trace dashboards. Owner: Priya Desai.
- Canary plan: enable protobuf for 5% of traffic with streaming disabled, measure p90/p99 and client error surface. Escalate to streaming+prefetch canary at 1% if stable. Owner: Jordan Kim.
- Follow-up benchmark: run the same matrix under multi-model mix (7b + 13b shard) and on Dedicated nodes to validate generalizability.

Appendix (raw traces snapshot pointers):
- sample-run-id: spline-run-20260503-19
- API traces: /traces/spline-run-20260503-19 (internal)

Notes to self: capture one small table comparing gzip(JSON) vs protobuf on client setups (mobile vs web) next iteration. Also add a micro-benchmark isolating only serialization to nail down CPU delta precisely.

End of runlog.
